titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 8/2021 (ޤައުމީ ޕޭމަންޓް ސިސްޓަމްގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This government bill, presented by the Makunudhoo MP, amends the National Payment System Act (Act No. 8/2021). It adds a new Article 50-1 that bans anyone without a licence or exemption from soliciting (offering or advertising) payment services to the public in the Maldives, and bans Maldivian payment operators from soliciting on behalf of unlicensed foreign providers. The Maldives Monetary Authority can fine anyone who breaks these rules between MVR 100,000 and MVR 10,000,000. The bill also rewrites Article 50(a) so that banks and parties exempted by the Authority under Article 18 are not caught by the licensing rule, and rewrites Article 15 to let system operators set up or join companies, partnerships and joint ventures to run systems or provide payment services.
whyItMatters: Foreign or unlicensed payment apps and services could no longer be marketed to people in the Maldives, and local payment firms that promote them could face fines of up to MVR 10 million.
keyProvisions: Article 15 is rewritten: operators keep their existing powers (owning or running systems, clearing and settlement, holding collateral, giving intraday liquidity), and a new Article 15(b) lets them form, or become shareholders or partners in, a company, partnership or joint venture to run a system or provide payment services.

Article 50(a) is rewritten: no one may provide payment services or run a payment system in the Maldives without a licence or permit from the Authority, except banks under Article 18(b), parties or activities the Authority has exempted under Article 18, and system operators under Article 18(a). No one may claim to offer such services without a licence.
New Article 50-1(a) bars anyone other than licensed providers, banks and exempted parties from soliciting payment services, whether in the Maldives or elsewhere, directly or through an intermediary.

New Article 50-1(b) and (c) bar anyone running a payment system or service in the Maldives from soliciting on behalf of a party outside the Maldives, unless that foreign party is itself licensed under the Act, a bank under Article 18(b), or exempted by the Authority.
New Article 50-1(d) lets the Authority fine anyone who breaks these rules between MVR 100,000 and MVR 10,000,000.

New Article 50-1(e) defines soliciting as offering, advertising or inviting the Maldivian public, or part of it, to take up a payment service or make an agreement for one, and 50-1(f) lets the Authority set out which specific acts count as soliciting. The amendment takes effect once ratified and published in the Government Gazette (clause 4).
whoIsAffected: Payment service providers and system operators in the Maldives, foreign payment companies marketing to Maldivians, and the Maldives Monetary Authority, which gains new fining powers.
statedReasons: The note says the Maldives Monetary Authority already licenses companies to run payment systems and provide payment services under Act No. 8/2021, and the bill adds rules to the law banning the solicitation of payment services and setting penalties for it.
